e.etymology: A Scandinavian surname from Old Norse byr, farm, and a spelling of the Danish and Swedish name Bo, from Old Norse bua, to dwell. In the US it is often chosen as another way to write Bo or Beau.
From the Hindi word suhana, pleasant or lovely, which goes back to a Sanskrit word for shining and beautiful.

e.meaning: strength (Hebrew); also short for Oscar or Oswald
e.etymology: In English a short form of Oscar, Oswald and Osborne. As a Hebrew name Oz means strength or might. Since 1900 it has also been the name of L. Frank Baum's magical land.

assoc.t: the magical land of The Wizard of Oz
Dr. Oz, TV doctor Mehmet Oz

e.etymology: An early Arabic name of uncertain root. It was borne by Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, a leader of Mecca in the Prophet Muhammad's time, and by the 8th-century scholar Sufyan al-Thawri.
A recent spelling in the family of Cohen, Koen and the surname Cowan; which of these a family has in mind varies.
A recent name used mainly in Mexican American families. Its source is not established.
A short modern name, used on its own or as a clipping of names ending in -ryn such as Kathryn, Taryn and Camryn.
A respelling of Lakelyn, a recent American coinage that joins the word lake to the popular -lyn ending.

e.meaning: a short tale that teaches a lesson
e.etymology: The English word for a short story with a moral, from Latin fabula, story. It joined other storytelling words such as Story, Saga and Poet as a given name in the 2020s.
A surname whose use as a first name follows NFL brothers Travis and Jason Kelce. It sounds like Kelsey to most people, though the family's own traditional pronunciation is one syllable.
namesakes: Travis Kelce (Kansas City Chiefs tight end)
Jason Kelce (former Philadelphia Eagles center and podcaster)

assoc.t: NFL brothers Travis and Jason Kelce

e.etymology: A respelling of Jakari, a modern American coinage in the Ja- family of names.

e.meaning: blend of Maria and Luisa; linked to Latin maris, of the sea
e.etymology: An Italian and Spanish contraction of Maria Luisa or Maria Isabel. Like Marissa, it is often connected with Latin maris, of the sea.
namesakes: Marisa Tomei (Oscar-winning actress in My Cousin Vinny)

e.meaning: short for Clifford, ford by a cliff
e.etymology: A short form of Clifford or Clifton, English place names built on Old English clif, a cliff or steep slope.
namesakes: Cliff Huxtable (the father on The Cosby Show)
Cliff Clavin (the mail carrier on Cheers)

e.etymology: An English surname taken up as a first name mostly among Latter-day Saints, in honor of church leader Dallin H. Oaks, who was himself named for Utah sculptor Cyrus Dallin.
From French Evelyne, the French form of Evelyn. Evelyn goes back through an English surname to the Norman women's name Aveline.

e.meaning: personal charm; from Greek for a gift of grace
e.etymology: The English word for compelling personal charm, from Greek kharisma, a gift or favor freely given.
namesakes: Charisma Carpenter (actress in Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Angel)

e.meaning: Armenian place name; in Welsh use, a form of taran, thunder
e.etymology: In Armenian it comes from Taron, a historic region west of Lake Van. Welsh actor Taron Egerton's name is a form of taran, the Welsh word for thunder.
namesakes: Taron Egerton (Welsh actor who played Elton John in Rocketman)

e.etymology: A spelling of Casey, from the Irish surname O Cathasaigh, descendant of Cathasach, a name meaning watchful. The K spellings also echo the initials K.C.
The Greek and Latin form of Hebrew Zekharyah, Yahweh has remembered. It is the New Testament spelling used for the father of John the Baptist.
A spelling of Jazlyn, an American coinage that joins the Jaz- of Jasmine, here written like the word jazz, to the -lyn ending.
A spelling of Nico that keeps the double c of Italian Niccolo, the form of Nicholas, from Greek nike, victory, and laos, people.
A modern American name in the family of Cambrie and Kambree, which appear to be shortened from Cambria, the Latin name for Wales.
From Sanskrit ekam, one. In Sikh use it points to the oneness of God, and like most Sikh names it is given to both boys and girls.
A respelling of Cruz, the Spanish word for cross and a common Spanish surname, written here like the English word cruise.

e.meaning: he lives; the Arabic form of John
e.etymology: A spelling of Yahya, the name of John the Baptist in the Quran. It matches the Arabic verb yahya, he lives, and corresponds to Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious.
A modern American name that joins Bren-, as in Brenna and Brenda, to the -leigh ending; a sister form of Brinley and Brynlee.
A short name with several sources: Japanese Rai, written with characters such as the one for thunder, and the Indian title and surname Rai, from raja, king.
From Japanese hinata, a sunny spot, built on hi, sun, and an old word for direction. As a name it is written with various kanji and is given to both girls and boys in Japan.
namesakes: Hinata Hyuga (character in the anime Naruto)
Shoyo Hinata (hero of the volleyball anime Haikyu!!)

assoc.t: Hinata Hyuga of the anime Naruto
Shoyo Hinata, hero of the volleyball anime Haikyu!!

e.etymology: An English surname for someone who lived by oak trees, and the plural of the tree word. It follows Oakley and Oaklyn into use as a first name.
